CHOSEN, in this order:
- (d) a per-node check on every write, with the fingerprint served on every read → req:every-read-hands-out-a-nodes-fingerprint-and-every-write-can-require-it.
- Per-agent identity, subagents and the flo2 gateway included → req:every-agent-working-a-design-is-its-own-claimant-subagents-included, with flo2's half req:the-gateway-gives-each-calling-agent-its-own-seat.
- Then (c): a write inside another agent's claim goes through and names the holder, at one hop → req:a-write-in-another-agents-claim-lands-and-names-who-holds-it.

NOT CHOSEN: (a) and (b), islands that refuse writes. The study found:
- 137 of 150 simulated warnings fell on a session's own subagents.
- An island at depth 2 covers 23% of other agents' edits on reflow2's design (98% for file records).
- No recorded collision would have been prevented.
- They cannot be built soundly until identity and liveness are fixed.

So dec:advisory-concurrency stands and was not reopened. The CONTRADICTS edge drawn at capture, which applied only to (a) and (b), was retracted with this settlement.","decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, dev_reflow2 hub session, 2026-09-29, recalling an old idea:

"have a brainstorming idea from a long time ago about carving out 'islands' in the graph for who is working what. This was kind of to prevent to agents from trying to work the same area of the graph at the same time. I believe the islands were determined by blast radius. Potentially, an agent can mark which areas of a design graph it is working so that other agents don't try to work on the same area (trying to prevent cases where two agents try to update the same nodes simultaneously). I suppose that reading anything on the graph is fine at anytime, it is more a mechanism that if an agent is editing a node/edge in the graph, it should do a 'blast radius' and no other agent can write in that blast radius until the agent releases it back."

═══ WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT OR SETTLED ═══
- THE ISLAND EXISTS AS A CLAIM. cap:cluster-claims (claim_region / release_claim / claim_report) marks a region computed from a seed and a depth, through the same traversal propagate_from uses, so the region follows the design as it changes. Reads are never affected.
- WRITE-BLOCKING WAS DECIDED AGAINST. dec:advisory-concurrency (accepted 2026-07-25): "Seats coordinate by announcement and provable order, never by exclusion". A claim is pinned by a test as not a lock: nothing consults one before a write, and overlap is reported, never prevented.
- BUT THAT DECISION'S PREMISE MOVED ON 2026-09-27 (fact:the-no-lock-decisions-premise-was-retired-2026-09-27-2026-09-29). It relied on git (claims published by push, crossings settled by git order) and on dec:multi-writer-architecture, which is now superseded. Sharing through git is retired: every writer now reaches a design through one server, which could check a claim at the moment of a write.
- THE SAME-NODE COLLISION ALREADY HAS A NARROW GUARD. cap:a-write-can-be-conditional-on-what-was-read: create_node refuses a write when the node changed since the caller read it (expected_content_hash). The typed tools (add_decision, add_requirement, ...) do not carry it yet, and that capability names this as the next question.

═══ THE OPTIONS ═══
(a) ISLANDS AS YOU PUT THEM. A write inside another session's claimed region is refused, naming who holds it, until they release it. ⚠️ Not a live option unless you reopen dec:advisory-concurrency, which is your call.
(b) ISLANDS WITH A LEASE. As (a), but a claim lapses unless its session keeps renewing it, so a crashed or disconnected agent cannot strand ground. ⚠️ Also needs dec:advisory-concurrency reopened.
(c) WARN, DON'T BLOCK. The write lands, and the reply names the claim and who holds it. The holder is told on their next call. Compatible with the accepted decision: it is still an announcement, just made at the one moment an agent is guaranteed to look. The cheapest option, since claims and regions already exist and only the write path has to ask.
(d) NO REGION, GUARD THE NODE. Carry the "what I read" check to every write tool, so a second simultaneous edit to the same node is refused instead of silently winning. Compatible. About ten tool surfaces. This is the narrowest answer to the hazard you named ("two agents try to update the same nodes simultaneously").
These combine. (c)+(d) together need no reopening.

═══ FOR ISLANDS ═══
- The main objection to enforcing, "there is no server to consult", no longer holds (see the finding above).
- The agents here are autonomous. An advisory claim only works if the other agent reads claim_report first, and nothing makes it do so. A refusal is the only form that needs no reading.

═══ AGAINST, recorded beside it ═══
- 🛑 LIVENESS IS MEASURED WRONG, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. On 2026-09-22 two active sessions' claims both read `gone` (fact:two-active-sessions-claims-both-read-gone-2026-09-22). An idle session silently takes a NEW seat (fact:root-cause-an-idle-session-expires-and-the-proxy-silently-takes-a-new-seat-so-live-claims-read-gone). Under (a), that agent would be locked out of its own island. Under (b), its island would lapse while it is still working. Enforcement is only as safe as liveness, so liveness comes first either way.
- ISLAND SIZE IS UNMEASURED. A blast radius at the default depth (2) from a well-connected node may cover a large share of a 6,000-node design. One such island would make every other agent wait. Measure the typical region size before choosing (a) or (b).
- A BLOCKED AUTONOMOUS AGENT HAS NOTHING GOOD TO DO. It can stop, wait, or ask a person who may be across the country. dec:advisory-concurrency's own evidence: "timidity starves the pool". Somebody also has to be able to break a stale island, and whoever can is the real authority, which needs a rule.
- ISLANDS DO NOT CATCH A DECISION MADE ON A STALE READ. Reads stay free, so an agent can read inside someone's island and write outside it on what it read. Neither islands nor (d) catch that unless the read travels with the write.

═══ WHERE IT WOULD LIVE ═══
In reflow2, on the write path every server shares. flo2 only serves it. flo2's proposed dashboard page could draw the islands, which is a pointer, not a second copy.","kind":"exploratory","name":"OPEN — should an agent editing the design mark its blast radius as an "island" that no other agent may write in until it releases it?","rationale":"Recorded as an open question, not a proposal.
